domain: vehicle roadworthiness testing / recurrent inspection outcomes
prediction_question: For a vehicle with at least one completed MOT test, will its next MOT test end in an initial failure (test_result F, or PRS - pass only after rectification at the station) rather than a clean pass, given only what is known up to and including its previous completed test?
prediction_time: The completion instant of the vehicle's previous test (completed_date in the prior test's row). Features are the vehicle's static attributes (make, model, colour, fuel_type, cylinder_capacity, first_use_date, test class) plus its full prior-test history (test dates, intervals, test types including NT/RT, prior results, mileage and mileage deltas, prior defect-item categories from the companion failure-item files). The next test's own fields (test_result, its test_mileage, its completed_date, its defect items) are the label source and never ship as features.
target_definition: Binary from the documented test_result field of the next test: positive if test_result is F or PRS - the DfT/DVSA documented 'initial failure' definition ('Initial failure rate = (Test Fail Results + Test PRS Results) / Total Tests', MOT Testing Data User Guide; the same definition drives the published DVSA/MOT/01 statistical tables). Negative if P. Abandoned/aborted codes (ABR, ABA - measured present at <0.6%) are excluded or handled at construction, to be decided and documented there.

Publisher caveats to carry onto any release, read from the CKAN notes 2026-10-19: 'This data set comes from data held by the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA). It is not classed as an official statistic'; the 2018 MOT regime change affected the information presented; the 2017 file was revised in June 2022 to include missing test results.
Vehicle identity is pseudonymised by the publisher (vehicle_id is a pseudonym over registration+VIN) - measured in the row sample; no personal data ships.
split_strategy: Temporal on the PREDICTION INSTANT (the prior completed class-4 test's date, the latest shipped knowable date): train priors 2009-01-01..2018-12-31, eval 2019-01-01..2021-12-31, holdout 2022-01-01..2023-11-30. CHANGED from the original next-test-year windows (train next-tests 2010-2018 / eval 2019-2021 / holdout 2022-2024) BEFORE any construction or score: the gate checks split windows against the declared time_column, and the next test's date is label-side timing information that cannot ship, so next-test-year windows are unverifiable from the rows; prior-year windows keep every check coherent with available data (label years shift ~+1, boundary lead-time overlap documented). Right-censoring cutoff: priors on/after 2023-12-01 are excluded wholesale (counted) so no row needs a next test beyond the 2024-12 data end - the excluded tail is exactly where short-gap post-failure retests would otherwise survive an annual-cycle censoring and bias prevalence. Population bounds (all pre-registered before any score): class 4 only (both sides of every pair; other classes counted and skipped), vehicles deterministically hash-sampled md5(vehicle_id) mod 1000 == 0 (~0.1%, outcome-independent, fixed before any split), completed tests only (ABR/ABA <0.6% measured - excluded from both sides and counted), pairs are consecutive completed class-4 tests in (test_date, completed_date, file order) after dedup of exact duplicate projected rows (test_id is NOT unique - measured 2026-10-19). Tests 2005-2008 are prior-history priming only. vehicle_id ships as a declared high-cardinality feature and is the event/cluster key; the runner id column is row_key (vehicle_id + pair ordinal, unique by construction).

measurements.cross_check_against_published_summary_pr: Prefix initial-fail 22.1% / final-fail 17.7% (August 2024, all classes, predominantly class 4) against the publisher's DVSA/MOT/01: FY2025-26 classes 3&4 initial 27.51% / final 22.30%, classes 1&2 13.40%, class 7 34.00%. Same magnitude and class ordering (August is a historically lenient month and the prefix mixes classes); no contradiction.
measurements.extraction_cost: Measured on the coordinator class: the whole shape measurement was ~14 ranged requests / ~4.5 MB / seconds. Construction is worker-scale: 1.53 GB compressed per year (2024 measured; other years labelled estimates) and ~7.7 GB uncompressed per year, so a 2010-2024 build is roughly 23 GB download and ~115 GB uncompressed processing - ESTIMATE derived from the single measured year; re-measure one more year on the worker before committing to the full window. Bounding to class 4 plus adjacent classes cuts this sharply.

construction_preflight_2026_11_05.source_access: CKAN package_show re-read 2026-11-05 (both datasets OGL v3.0): DfT package carries 40 resources including all 20 per-year RESULT files - test_result_2005..2016.txt.gz and dft_test_result_2017..2022.zip at data.dft.gov.uk/anonymised-mot-test/test_data/, dft_test_result_2023.zip mirrored at the DVSA S3 origin, MOT+testing+data+results+(2024).zip at the DVSA S3 origin. Failure-item files exist per year but are NOT used in v1: they join by test_id, which is measured NOT unique (6,336 repeat values in one month's prefix), so the join is ambiguous; the reduction is documented, not silent.
construction_preflight_2026_11_05.range_header_finding: MEASURED 2026-11-05: data.dft.gov.uk IGNORES Range headers - a ranged probe of dft_test_result_2019.zip streamed ~1.08 GB before being killed; the coordinator-side probe was aborted and no DfT bulk transfer happens on the coordinator. Consequence: DfT-era schemas (2005-2022) cannot be pre-measured from the coordinator and are measured BY the build itself, which records every observed header/delimiter in summary.json and fails loudly on an unmappable schema. The DVSA S3 origin answers ranged reads (2026-10-19 measurement unchanged).
construction_preflight_2026_11_05.vintage_pin: The 2024 zip is byte-pinned to the 2026-10-19 measurement: 1,531,265,132 bytes, 12 monthly members test_result_202401..202412.csv, 15-column header verified verbatim; the build asserts all three and refuses on drift. The other 19 files were never fetched before, so the build RECORDS their sha256 as the construction vintage pin (a rebuild must match).
construction_preflight_2026_11_05.dry_run_2026_11_05: Full build+gate+accept+score machinery exercised on synthetic fixtures spanning all three file eras (headerless pipe 2005-2008, headered pipe 2009-2016, single-member zips 2017-2023, 12-member pinned 2024 zip), including duplicate rows, ABR rows, other-class rows and the censoring cutoff. Gate 1.5.0: 45/45 PASS on the synthetic extract; --accept ACCEPTED; the declared cross-row probe measured the blind-join exposure (synthetic eval coverage 420/570 rows, 0 mismatches - a later pair's prior_initial_fail equals the earlier pair's label by construction, which is exactly the exposure the probe exists to measure); access is isolated_rows. Fixture numbers are NOT findings and are never quoted.
construction_preflight_2026_11_05.pre_registered_triad: Deciding members (written before any construction or score, mirrored in source/score.py): persistence_prior_result (the prior test's own initial-fail flag - the last observed outcome), calendar_make_week (train-estimated rate per make x ISO week-of-year, make then global fallback), vehicle_train_rate (train-estimated rate per vehicle_id - the panel identity prior). Supplementary: global_rate (degenerate, Brier only), majority_class accuracy. DECIDING RULE: headroom ONLY if the full model beats EVERY deciding member with a cluster-aware paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero in the model's favour AND the model's own cluster-bootstrap AUC CI lies entirely above 0.5; triad dominance -> DROP. Clusters = vehicle_id. Per-prior-year reporting mandatory (May-2018 regime change; 2020-21 pandemic test extensions).
construction_preflight_2026_11_05.schema_risk: The 2005-2022 file schemas are unmeasured until the build runs (Range ignored at DfT). The build maps by header name with a positional fallback for headerless eras, asserts test_result values within {P,F,PRS,ABR,ABA}, requires a non-zero class-4 sampled row count per year, and records every observed header; an unmappable schema fails the job loudly with the evidence in the collected logs (one bounded worker cycle at risk, accepted deliberately).

measurements.artifact_allowance_check_2026_11_05: PRE-COMPLETION CHECK (written 2026-11-05 19:2xZ, while dvsa-mot-build-001 was still running, BEFORE any outcome existed). The launched job declares max_artifact_mb = 8, and workers/upload.py refuses the WHOLE staging upload (reports included) when the bytes under /output plus source.tar plus container.log exceed that allowance. MEASURED inputs: 2024 source year = 7,667,648,876 B uncompressed (~64M rows at the prefix-measured ~120 B/row); first-4MB prefix of test_result_202408.csv = 34,924 rows with 19,328 distinct vehicle_ids; shipped extract = 21 plain-CSV columns. ESTIMATE (not a measurement): the md5 mod 1000 == 0 vehicle sample keeps ~0.1% of a multi-ten-million vehicle panel, so the pair panel plausibly lands in the hundreds-of-thousands of rows (~30-130 MB extract) - every other candidate in the catalog sized max_artifact_mb to its extract (austin 131 MB extract -> 400; msha 3.38 GB -> 4200; za-cct 8.4 MB -> 24), while this job's 8 MiB supports only ~60k rows at ~128 B/row. PREDICTION, not a finding: if the extract exceeds the allowance, publish() raises UploadError('Artifacts exceed job allowance') and NOTHING uploads - but executor.py still embeds /output/summary.json (<= 64 KiB) in /opt/scout/result.json and `worker collect` is designed to fetch exactly that, so the measured row counts, per-file sizes and the 19-file vintage sha256 pins survive for a correctly-sized rebuild. RESPONSE PRE-REGISTERED: one corrected rebuild (dvsa-mot-build-002, new job ID per the immutable-bundle rule) with max_artifact_mb sized from the collected per-file bytes with >= 2.5x headroom; construction logic unchanged - this is a job-descriptor defect, not a build defect; the gate/triad then rerun deterministically on the rebuilt bytes. If collect instead shows a clean upload, this entry is void and the baseline proceeds as recorded.
measurements.build_failure_2015_abrve_2026_11_05: MEASURED on the worker (dvsa-mot-build-001, container.log collected to .factory/dvsa-mot-build-001/ and preserved in staging release 435609197): the build fetched and parsed 2005-2014 cleanly - per-year rows_seen / class4 / sampled (md5 mod 1000 == 0): 2005 7,499,744/7,113,089/7,101; 2006 32,014,080/30,302,568/30,572; 2007 33,591,238/31,803,974/31,948; 2008 34,439,132/32,591,753/32,500; 2009 35,436,943/33,529,083/33,506; 2010 36,134,920/34,179,326/34,097; 2011 36,849,154/34,790,696/35,074; 2012 36,846,342/34,831,846/34,872; 2013 37,361,925/35,346,508/35,295; 2014 37,493,825/35,458,346/35,635. Per-year result histograms for P/F/PRS/ABR/ABA recorded in the log; ABR+ABA stays ~0.55-0.7% (the <0.6% pre-launch estimate was correct in scale). FAILURE at source_2015.txt.gz seq 18757: test_result='ABRVE' (row: test_id 1574076421, vehicle_id 192184530, test_date 2015-07-03, class 4, NT, test_mileage empty, postcode SK, VOLKSWAGEN GOLF PLUS, RED, DI, 1896, first_use 2006-07-07, completed_date empty). All other fields are well-formed, so this is a source VALUE anomaly, not a delimiter/parse shift; the empty mileage and completed_date match the abandoned-row shape. 'ABRVE' is not in the documented result-code set. CONSEQUENCES, both measured/derived: (1) the sampled panel is ~34-35k completed class-4 tests per year, so priors 2009-2023 is ~500k tests -> ~450-490k pair rows -> ~57-65 MB extract at the 21-column ~128 B/row - the launch's max_artifact_mb=8 would ALSO have refused the upload (see artifact_allowance_check_2026_11_05, directionally confirmed); (2) 2015-2024 result-value inventories remain unmeasured because the build died at 2015 (Range is ignored at data.dft.gov.uk, so a bounded coordinator-side probe is impossible - the repair must inventory them on the worker).
